story.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Expands to Sixth Province Amid Rising Death Toll
story.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, following the death of a man who traveled from Haut-Uele. The World Health Organization has indicated that this outbreak is on track to become the deadliest in history, surpassing the previous record of over 11,000 fatalities from a decade ago. Currently, more than 2,100 deaths have been reported out of over 4,500 cases.

timeline_highlights.title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Claims Over 2,000 Lives, Marked as Fastest Growing on Record
timeline_highlights.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo reports that at least 2,000 people have died in its ongoing Ebola outbreak, which is now recognized as the fastest growing on record. As of the latest updates, there have been 4,381 confirmed cases across five provinces. The outbreak reportedly began months before it was officially declared in May, complicating response efforts due to factors such as rebel conflict and infrastructure challenges.

timeline_highlights.title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Could Become Deadliest in History, WHO Warns
timeline_highlights.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Congo, declared on May 15, has already resulted in over 2,000 deaths and thousands of additional reported cases. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus indicated that if the current trend continues, this outbreak could surpass the deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded during the West African epidemic from 2014 to 2016.

related_stories.title: US Missionary Kevin Rideout Released After Kidnapping in Niger
related_stories.summary: Kevin Rideout, an American missionary kidnapped in Niger last October, has been released after nine months in captivity. He is reported to be in good health and is currently in the care of US officials. His organization, SIM International, stated that he would soon be reunited with his family.

related_stories.title: USS George Washington Deploys to Middle East Amid Concerns Over USS Lincoln's Conditions
related_stories.summary: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier is en route to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has faced reports of declining mental health and supply issues among its crew during its record 260-day deployment. Some sailors aboard the Lincoln have reportedly attempted self-harm due to the conditions. However, U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has disputed these reports, calling them misrepresented, and senators are calling for an investigation into the situation.

related_stories.title: Zambians Vote in Presidential Election Amid Economic Concerns
related_stories.summary: Zambians voted on Thursday in a presidential election that tests the economic reforms of incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema. Approximately 8 million registered voters also selected members of Parliament and local councilors. Vote counting is currently underway, with results expected on Monday.
